content.text:
Repaired RouteKit's zone-key behavior.

## Files changed
- `routekit/zones.py` — the single implementation change. Added an `import re` and a compiled `_WHITESPACE_RUN = re.compile(r"\s+")`, and updated `canonical_zone` to: `return _WHITESPACE_RUN.sub("-", value.strip().lower())`. This adds the missing hyphen-replacement step on top of the existing strip/lower. Because `labels.py` (`zone_label`) and `manifest.py` (`build_manifest`, used by the CLI) both call `canonical_zone`, the CLI manifest output and shipment labels now share the identical behavior with zero changes to those files. The CLI command name (`manifest`) and JSON field name (`zone_key`) are untouched.

## Behavior verified
- Lowercase keys, strip leading/trailing whitespace, collapse every run of internal whitespace to a single hyphen, preserve existing hyphens and digits.
- All four acceptance examples confirmed via CLI and direct calls:
  1. `" North\tDock "` → `north-dock`
  2. `canonical_zone(" East \n Gate ")` → `east-gate`
  3. `zone_label(" West  Wing ")` → `zone:west-wing`
  4. `" SOUTH-2 "` → `south-2`
- Extra edge cases checked: multiple mixed whitespace runs (`a-b-c`), preserved hyphens (`already-here`), preserved digits (`zone-123-4x`), and whitespace-only / leading-trailing padding cases.

## Tests run and outcome
Ran the existing command from the repo root, before and after the change:
`python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v`

- Before: 4 tests ran, 3 FAILED (cli, labels, internal-whitespace), 1 ok.
- After: 4 tests ran, 4 passed — **Ran 4 tests, OK** (test_manifest_whitespace, test_shared_zone_normalization, test_existing_hyphenated_key, test_internal_whitespace).

## Notes / uncertainty
- The `\s+` regex matches whitespace (space, tab, newline, etc.) but not hyphens or digits, so it satisfies the "preserve existing hyphens and digits" requirement.
- One caveat during manual CLI checks in the shell: single-quoted arguments pass literal backslash sequences (`\t`, `\n`) rather than real control characters, so I re-ran the CLI verification through Python with actual tab/newline characters in the input strings — those confirmed the same results as the automated test suite. No functional uncertainty remains; the full suite passes.
